set.question: Which sentence gives a cause?
options: La ciudad cambió debido a la falta de agua. [The city changed due to the lack of water.]
La ciudad cambió; por eso, hay menos agua. [The city changed; that is why there is less water.]
La ciudad cambiará en los próximos años. [The city will change in the coming years.]

set.question: Which sentence builds an argument with more than one connector?
options: La medida es útil porque reduce los costes; además, protege el medio ambiente. [The measure is useful because it reduces costs; furthermore, it protects the environment.]
La medida que aprobó el ayuntamiento es muy útil para todos los vecinos. [The measure the city council approved is very useful for all the neighbours.]
La nueva propuesta reduce mucho los costes del transporte público de la ciudad. [The new proposal greatly reduces the public transport costs of the city.]

set.question: Which sentence gives a cause?
options: La ciudad cambió debido a la falta de agua. [The city changed due to the lack of water.]
La ciudad cambió; por eso, hay menos agua. [The city changed; that is why there is less water.]
La ciudad cambió; sin embargo, sigue igual. [The city changed; however, it stays the same.]

set.question: Which sentence combines contrast and consequence?
options: Era caro; sin embargo, lo compramos, por eso tuvimos que ahorrar. [It was expensive; however, we bought it, so we had to save.]
Era caro; sin embargo, decidimos esperar un poco más de tiempo. [It was expensive; however, we decided to wait a little longer.]
Compramos una casa nueva, por eso tuvimos que ahorrar mucho tiempo. [We bought a new house, so we had to save for a long time.]

set.question: Which sentence best integrates the unit?
options: El proyecto es necesario porque hay un problema; sin embargo, debe ser económico para que pueda funcionar. [The project is necessary because there is a problem; however, it must be economical so that it can work.]
El proyecto nuevo ya existe y cuenta con el apoyo de todos los vecinos de la ciudad. [The new project already exists and has the support of all the city's neighbours.]
Hay un problema de transporte en las calles principales del centro de la ciudad. [There is a transport problem on the main streets of the city centre.]

set.question: Which sentence best shows a balanced argument?
options: La solución es cara; sin embargo, puede lograr buenos resultados y proteger el entorno. [The solution is expensive; however, it can achieve good results and protect the environment.]
La solución propuesta resulta muy cara, por eso consideramos que no es buena. [The proposed solution turns out very expensive, so we consider it is not good.]
La solución que aprobó el ayuntamiento es buena y muy conveniente para todos. [The solution the city council approved is good and very convenient for everyone.]

"lemma": "por lo tanto",

"lemma": "por esa razón",
      "translation": "for that reason",

old: "Use *porque*, *debido* a, por, ya que and *como* to explain causes and reasons."
new: "You know *porque* and *debido a* (B1 Unit 11). *Ya que* and *como* also give a cause: use them to explain causes and reasons."

old: "*Como* meaning 'since' only works at the front of the sentence — Como *había* poco *tiempo*, salimos temprano — while *porque* and *ya* *que* can introduce the reason in either position."
new: "*Como* meaning 'since' opens the sentence (*Como había poco tiempo, salimos temprano*), while *porque* and *ya que* usually follow the result: *Salimos temprano porque había poco tiempo.*"

old: "Use por *eso*, por lo *tanto*, así que and *como* *resultado* to explain consequences."
new: "You know *por eso* (A2 Unit 5) and *así que* (B1 Unit 1). *Como resultado* and *por esa razón* work in the same way: use them to explain consequences."

old: "Faltaba transporte; por lo tanto, los comerciantes tuvieron problemas."
new: "Faltaba transporte; por esa razón, los comerciantes tuvieron problemas."

old: "There was a lack of transport; therefore, the shopkeepers had problems."
new: "There was a lack of transport; for that reason, the shopkeepers had problems."

old: "These connectors point forward from cause to result, the reverse direction of *porque*: the problem comes first, then por *eso*, así *que* or como *resultado* introduces what followed."
new: "These connectors point forward from cause to result, the reverse of *porque*: the cause comes first, then *por eso*, *así que* or *como resultado* introduces the result."

old: "Use pero, *sin* *embargo*, *aunque*, a *pesar* de and en cambio to contrast ideas and concede a point."
new: "You know *aunque* and *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28. This lesson adds *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + a full clause, and *pese a*, to concede a difficulty and go on."

old: "Aunque era difícil, continuamos."
new: "A pesar de las dificultades, continuamos."

old: "Although it was difficult, we continued."
new: "Despite the difficulties, we continued."

old: "Era caro; sin embargo, decidimos comprarlo."
new: "A pesar de que era caro, decidimos comprarlo."

old: "It was expensive; however, we decided to buy it."
new: "Although it was expensive, we decided to buy it."

old: "A *pesar* *de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive (a pesar de *ser* caro), never a conjugated verb the way *aunque* is — for a full clause after it you'd need a *pesar* de *que*."
new: "*A pesar de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive (*a pesar de ser caro*); before a full clause use *a pesar de que* (*a pesar de que era caro*), with the indicative when the fact is real. *Pese a* means the same: *pese a las dificultades*."

old: "Use *para*, para *que* and con el *fin* de to explain purposes and objectives."
new: "You know *para* (A2 Unit 30) and *para que* + subjunctive (B1 Unit 7). *Con el fin de* + infinitive also gives a purpose: use them to explain purposes and objectives."

old: "Salimos temprano para que no hubiera problemas."
new: "Salimos temprano todos los días para que no haya problemas."

old: "We left early so that there would be no problems."
new: "We leave early every day so that there are no problems."

old: "*Para* + infinitive works when the same person studies and benefits (Estudiamos para *mejorar*), but once the purpose belongs to someone else you need para *que* + subjunctive: salimos temprano para *que* no *hubiera* problemas."
new: "*Para* + infinitive works when the same person acts and benefits (*estudiamos para mejorar*); when the purpose belongs to someone else you need *para que* + subjunctive: *salimos temprano para que no haya problemas*."

old: "Combine causal, consequential, contrastive and purposive connectors to build a clear argument."
new: "You know every connector here: causes (*porque*, *debido a*), consequences (*por eso*, *así que*), contrast (*aunque*, *sin embargo*, *a pesar de*) and purpose (*para que*). Combine them to build a clear argument."

old: "A semicolon before the connector (es *cara*; sin *embargo*...) reads as tighter and more formal than starting a new sentence — worth using once you're chaining several connectors in one argument."
new: "A semicolon before the connector (*es cara; sin embargo...*) reads as tighter and more formal than starting a new sentence."
